name: France
maturity_rationale: Scored above Germany (anchor 2) and below Japan (anchor 4), on space specificity rather than general warmth. Germany's 2 reflects CSpO co-membership and strong capability with no bilateral government-to-government space instrument; France clears that bar three times over: a ministerial Declaration of Intent on military space cooperation naming earth observation, SSA and milsatcom (EV-FRANCE-10), an ASA-CNES MoU published 30 April 2024 (EV-FRANCE-12), and a leaders-endorsed roadmap with a standing space-cooperation chapter including an explicit SSA commitment (EV-FRANCE-11) — on top of shared CSpO membership (EV-FRANCE-08) and, since 14 October 2024, shared MNF-OOD membership (EV-FRANCE-09). It stays below 4 because nothing beyond declared intent is evidenced: no operational data exchange, no combined space exercising, no liaison presence, no binding instrument; the entire space architecture is 2022-2024 vintage built during the post-AUKUS repair (EV-FRANCE-13, EV-FRANCE-14), and one round of collection found no implementation evidence under either space instrument. Intent-rich, operations-poor: 3/5, not scored higher precisely to avoid rewarding paper over practice.
one_line: France pairs Europe's most complete military-space capability and Pacific residency with a young, post-AUKUS-repair bilateral space architecture — a military-space Declaration of Intent, an ASA-CNES MoU and a roadmap space chapter — none of it yet evidenced as operationalised.

name: Italy
maturity_rationale: Scored level with Germany (2) and New Zealand (2), on space specificity. The Germany-2 condition — CSpO co-member, genuinely capable, but no bilateral government-to-government space instrument — holds for Italy almost exactly: CSpO member since December 2023 (EV-USSFCSPO-08), a full sovereign military space stack (EV-ITALY-07 to EV-ITALY-12), but the only bilateral instrument is a narrow agency-level statement of intent of 17 February 2020 'to consider' one ISS activity, with no evidenced follow-through (EV-ITALY-03, EV-ITALY-04). Italy arguably edges Germany on paper because its agency instrument is confirmed against the primary text where Germany's 2019 DLR letter remains TO_VERIFY, and DFAT declares a 'strong partnership' (EV-ITALY-02) — but declaratory warmth does not move the score, exactly as New Zealand's alliance-grade general relationship did not. Well short of Japan (4): no G2G space agreement, no defence-space instrument, no operational space cooperation, and a general defence relationship that produced its first exercise participation only in 2024 (EV-ITALY-17). Not a 1: the CSpO seat, the live instrument, founding co-signature of the Artemis Accords (EV-ITALY-13) and parallel DA-ASAT commitments (EV-ITALY-14) are real space-specific fabric. One-round baseline — score provisional pending a second round.
one_line: Italy is the inverse New Zealand: a full-stack military space power (sovereign SAR, milsatcom, optical ISR, a 2020 space command, a 2025 national space law, CSpO from December 2023) whose entire bilateral space channel with Australia is one dormant 2020 agency statement of intent.

name: Norway
maturity_rationale: Scored level with Germany (2) and New Zealand (2) on space specificity, not relationship warmth. Norway meets the Germany-anchor formula exactly: CSpO co-member (from December 2023, EV-NORWAY-04), genuinely capable in niche space lanes (ASBM HEO SATCOM with allied hosted payloads, EV-NORWAY-07/-08; world-leading polar ground segment, EV-NORWAY-11; sovereign orbital launch site, EV-NORWAY-13), but no bilateral government-to-government space instrument with Australia of any kind (EV-NORWAY-02). Two features pull in opposite directions and net out: the space-specific Australia track is even emptier than Germany's (no project-level touchpoints equivalent to DLR-TeraNet or Koonibba launches — nothing at all), while the materiel-industrial relationship is thicker than any other maturity-2 partner's (up to $850m Williamtown factory, GWEO strategic partnership, $142m JSM contract, reciprocal 2024 ministerial visits — EV-NORWAY-03/-16/-17) and Norway hosts CSpO senior officials in Oslo in December 2026 (EV-NORWAY-05). Not a 1: the shared CSpO seat plus real capability plus a warm ministerial channel exceed a bare-acquaintance score. Nowhere near Japan (4): no bilateral space instrument, no operational integration (not even MNF-OOD membership, EV-NORWAY-06), no space dialogue. One-round scoring; not to be ranked against two-round partners without a second round.
one_line: Capable niche space nation and Australia's fastest-growing missile-industrial partner — with a completely empty bilateral space rail; CSpO is the only shared space vehicle, and Oslo hosts its senior officials in December 2026.

name: Republic of Korea
maturity_rationale: Scored 3/5 on space specificity against the anchors (US=5, Japan=4, Germany=2, NZ=2). The ROK clears the bar that caps Germany and New Zealand at 2: a dedicated bilateral government-to-government space instrument exists — the December 2021 MoU on Space Cooperation for Peaceful Purposes with a standing annual Space Policy Dialogue (EV-ROK-02) — refreshed at agency level by the October 2025 KASA-ASA MoU and Statement of Intent (EV-ROK-03), and the 2015 defence Blueprint carries an explicit 'cooperate on space security' commitment (EV-ROK-04). It does not reach Japan's 4 because the defence-space lane is empty in practice: the ROK is not a CSpO member (EV-ROK-18), shares no operational or exercise-level space channel with Australia (EV-ROK-05), its allied military-space integration runs through the US bilateral and US-Japan-ROK trilateral lanes (EV-ROK-10, EV-ROK-12), and the bilateral space track located is civil-led with no evidence of military space data flows, combined space operations or a defence-space instrument. One-round baseline; do not inflate further without verifying the Space Policy Dialogue's actual cadence since 2022.
one_line: The inverse of the New Zealand finding: a partner with real bilateral space instruments (2021 Space MoU, annual Space Policy Dialogue, 2025 KASA-ASA MoU) and serious sovereign capability, but sitting outside CSpO — so Australia's defence-space architecture and the ROK's have no shared room to meet in.

name: Singapore
maturity_rationale: Scored 1/5 on space-specificity, deliberately below Germany (2) and New Zealand (2). Both anchors hold CSpO membership - a standing, space-specific operational vehicle shared with Australia - and were scored 2 despite having no bilateral space instrument. Singapore has neither the bilateral instrument NOR any allied space structure: it is not in CSpO and not in Five Eyes (EV-SINGAPORE-15), no ASA-OSTIn or other agency MoU could be evidenced (EV-SINGAPORE-14, -15), and the word 'space' is absent from CSP 2.0, the DFAT country brief and the 2023/2024 SAJMC communiques (EV-SINGAPORE-03, -04, -05, -06). The only space-specific overlap is multilateral and thin: OST, COPUOS and the Artemis Accords (EV-SINGAPORE-13). Singapore's genuine sovereign capability (TeLEOS-1/-2, EV-SINGAPORE-10, -11) and the alliance-depth general defence relationship (EV-SINGAPORE-02, -07) do not raise the score, because the score measures the space partnership, not capability or warmth - the same discipline applied to New Zealand. Not scored 0 because the shared Artemis Accords/COPUOS/OST membership and a live bilateral defence S&T channel (EV-SINGAPORE-02, -06) give real, citable touchpoints a first space initiative could use. One-round baseline; score provisional pending items 1-3 of the validation backlog - an actual ASA-OSTIn MoU, if confirmed, would move Singapore to 2.

The A$38bn/2036 investment line does not raise the score: announced money is not engagement.
